Map charged tRNAs to codons by direct cognate assignment; aggregate isodecoders and organisms as robust medians to form x. Residualize x against C and normalize the residual to d_resid4.
controls: The raw score is binding thermodynamics of charged tRNA, not tRNA abundance, codon usage, or ribosome dwell.
Amino-acid one-hot, tRNA supply, tRNA consensus, wobble class, f3/ramp, d_perp, GC, codon-pair, mRNA-stability, and ribosome-dwell scores are controls.
Reject if binding values correlate with tAI or gene copy after residualization.
Run charged-versus-uncharged exclusion audit: uncharged-tRNA controls must not produce the same SerSplit projection.
Run buffer/method leave-one-out audits.

candidate_axes.construction: For each standard-code sense codon, count phylogenetically deduplicated independent reassignment or ambiguous-assignment events in which that codon changes amino-acid meaning or becomes stop. Normalize as x_i=log((events_i+0.5)/(opportunities_i-events_i+0.5)), where opportunities are the number of screened independent clades in which the codon was observable. Residualize x against C plus codon-family degeneracy and stop-adjacency indicators; normalize the residual to d_resid4 if nonzero.
controls: Phylogenetic deduplication prevents one clade expansion from counting as many events.
GC, codon disappearance, tRNA loss/supply, wobble class, codon-pair effects, mRNA stability, and ribosome dwell are controls or exclusion reasons, not explanatory inputs.
Remove all stop codons from the tested 61-vector; stop-adjacency is a control only.
Repeat after excluding mitochondrial codes and after excluding bacterial/archaeal candidate recodings; projection must not be unique to one domain.
Negative control: randomize reassignment events across codons within equal degeneracy classes and recompute the projection.

Fit a neutral-context model from noncoding or fourfold-degenerate sites, subtract expected mutation burden, and aggregate the residual by codon to x. Residualize x against C plus explicit CpG/UpA and local trinucleotide mutability columns; normalize to d_resid4.
controls: The raw axis is DNA damage/repair or mutability residual, not translation efficiency, tRNA supply, ribosome dwell, mRNA stability, or codon-pair usage.

Exclude disease-enriched, splice-proximal, nonsense-adjacent, and overlapping functional elements.
Repeat in separate ancestry groups and in de novo-only data; the candidate is rejected if projection exists only in one ascertainment source.
Negative control: use intronic pseudo-codons in the same genes and reading-frame phases; they must not reproduce the SerSplit projection.

GENCODE or Ensembl CDS annotation: transcript sequence, codon, reading frame, exon, strand
COSMIC/PCAWG mutational-signature exposure table only as a control source, not as the raw axis

candidate_axes.name: synonymous_DNA_damage_repair_residual_axis

Negative control: shift CDS reading frame by +1 and +2 before codon aggregation; shifted pseudo-codons must not reproduce the projection.
Reject if SerSplit projection is driven by a single tissue, transcript family, or editable-base composition.

GTEx or ENCODE RNA-seq coverage/expression table for opportunity normalization
GENCODE or Ensembl CDS annotation with codon coordinate and reading frame
mRNA half-life and RNA-binding-protein annotation tracks used only as controls

candidate_axes.name: coding_RNA_editing_residual_axis

gene/transcript annotation for each MAVE library: CDS position, amino acid, codon context, expression construct, library design

data_sources: bounded 61-sense-codon synthetic DNA oligo panel with identical flanking sequence on both sides of the codon

LC-MS, primer-extension, nanopore, or sequencing readouts for UV dimerization, oxidative lesions, hydrolytic deamination, and alkylation under fixed exposure conditions

candidate_axes.audit_test: Apply TEST_U_SERSPLIT to the residual mutability axis after all DNA-context controls. Also report rho after removing CpG-containing codons and after matching UCN and AGY codons by genome-wide opportunity where possible.

Use only variants classified as synonymous in the locked transcript set; exclude codon changes affecting splice motifs or overlapping regulatory annotations. Fit a neutral-context model from noncoding or fourfold-degenerate sites, subtract expected mutation burden, and aggregate the residual by codon to x. Residualize x against C plus explicit CpG/UpA and local trinucleotide mutability columns; normalize to d_resid4.
controls: The raw axis is DNA damage/repair or mutability residual, not translation efficiency, tRNA supply, ribosome dwell, mRNA stability, or codon-pair usage.
GC1/GC2/GC3/total_GC, CpG, TpA/UpA, methylation, trinucleotide mutation opportunity, codon-pair scores, mRNA-stability scores, and dwell scores are controls.
Exclude disease-enriched, splice-proximal, nonsense-adjacent, and overlapping functional elements.
Repeat in separate ancestry groups and in de novo-only data; the candidate is rejected if projection exists only in one ascertainment source.
Negative control: use intronic pseudo-codons in the same genes and reading-frame phases; they must not reproduce the SerSplit projection.

de novo mutation or near-neutral pedigree mutation table with callable opportunity mask
GENCODE or Ensembl CDS annotation: transcript sequence, codon, reading frame, exon, strand
COSMIC/PCAWG mutational-signature exposure table only as a control source, not as the raw axis
candidate_axes.failure_mode: Fails if GC/CpG/trinucleotide context explains the residual, if coding selection or splice/regulatory overlap drives the score, if the 61-codon opportunity table is incomplete, or if SerSplit projection is absent in de novo mutation data.

candidate_axes.audit_test: Apply TEST_U_SERSPLIT to the editing residual axis. Report projections separately for A-to-I-only, C-to-U-only, and combined axes; only preregistered combined or replicated type-specific projections are considered candidate hits.
candidate_axes.construction: Map high-confidence RNA editing sites into CDS codons. For each sense codon, compute editing burden per callable expressed codon occurrence, separately for A-to-I and C-to-U, requiring minimum read depth and excluding known DNA variants. Normalize within tissue by expression, coverage, editable-base opportunity, and local sequence motif; combine tissues by median or random-effects meta-analysis to produce x. Residualize x against C plus expression, editable-base count, ADAR/APOBEC motif score, RBP density, and mRNA half-life; normalize residual to d_resid4.
controls: DNA SNPs and mapping-ambiguous sites are excluded.
mRNA stability, expression, coverage, local editing motif, GC, codon-pair, tRNA supply, f3/ramp, d_perp, wobble, and ribosome dwell are residualized or matched.
Run tissue leave-one-out and editing-type-specific audits.
Negative control: shift CDS reading frame by +1 and +2 before codon aggregation; shifted pseudo-codons must not reproduce the projection.
Reject if SerSplit projection is driven by a single tissue, transcript family, or editable-base composition.
data_sources: REDIportal, RADAR, or equivalent A-to-I and C-to-U RNA editing calls: genomic coordinate, transcript, editing type, editing level, coverage, tissue, strand
GTEx or ENCODE RNA-seq coverage/expression table for opportunity normalization
GENCODE or Ensembl CDS annotation with codon coordinate and reading frame
mRNA half-life and RNA-binding-protein annotation tracks used only as controls
candidate_axes.failure_mode: Fails if RNA editing burden is explained by editable-base composition, expression, mRNA half-life, local motifs, or mapping artifacts, or if coverage is insufficient for all 61 sense codons.
candidate_axes.name: coding_RNA_editing_residual_axis

candidate_axes.audit_test: Apply TEST_U_SERSPLIT to each preregistered modification-type residual and to the combined residual after Holm correction over modification types. No biological-axis claim is made from a single unreplicated modification source.
candidate_axes.construction: Map mRNA modification calls inside coding regions to codon identity and codon position. Normalize within study and tissue by expression, coverage, modification-calling platform, local motif score, and codon-position opportunity; aggregate across studies by robust median to obtain x. Residualize x against C plus mRNA half-life, predicted local structure, RBP motif density, and known modification motifs; normalize residual to d_resid4.
controls: mRNA stability and local RNA structure are controls, not the candidate axis.

Negative control: use UTR modification calls randomly assigned to CDS codons by expression-matched transcript; projection must vanish.

data_sources: RMBase, m6A-Atlas, DirectRMDB, or equivalent transcriptome modification calls: modification type, coordinate, transcript, tissue/cell type, confidence, stoichiometry if available

matched expression, mRNA half-life, local motif, and structure tracks used as controls
candidate_axes.failure_mode: Fails if modification calls are motif/GC/stability artifacts, if platform bias dominates, if events are too sparse for 61 codons, or if SerSplit projection is not replicated across independent mapping technologies.
candidate_axes.name: mRNA_base_modification_residual_axis

Residualize x against C plus assay-specific RNA-structure, codon-pair, mRNA-stability, and dwell covariates; normalize residual to d_resid4.
controls: Only synonymous substitutions are used; nonsynonymous and splice/regulatory variants are excluded.
Amino-acid identity, gene, protein position, assay, source codon, target codon, expression, codon-pair, mRNA stability, ribosome dwell, GC, wobble, tRNA supply, f3/ramp, and d_perp are controlled.
Leave-one-gene-family and leave-one-assay-type audits are required.
Negative control: permute synonymous scores within amino acid and gene while preserving codon counts; projection must vanish.
Reject if SerSplit projection is carried by one gene, one assay, or one codon substitution direction.
data_sources: MaveDB and ProteinGym synonymous variant tables: variant sequence, reference codon, alternate codon, score, raw counts, replicate ID, assay type, selection condition
gene/transcript annotation for each MAVE library: CDS position, amino acid, codon context, expression construct, library design
matched codon-pair, RNA-structure, mRNA-stability, and ribosome-profiling controls for each assayed gene where available
candidate_axes.failure_mode: Fails if MAVE coverage does not span all 61 codons, if effects are dominated by mRNA stability/codon-pair/dwell terms, if synonymous scores are too assay-specific, or if the model cannot identify codon effects separately from gene and position effects.

candidate_axes.audit_test: Apply TEST_U_SERSPLIT separately to each lesion chemistry and to any preregistered combined lesion axis. Report whether projection survives explicit GC and nearest-neighbor residualization.
candidate_axes.construction: Synthesize oligos in which only the central codon varies across the 61 sense codons and all flanking bases, concentration, exposure, time, temperature, and buffer are identical. For each damage chemistry, estimate lesion rate per molecule from raw replicate counts. Within chemistry and replicate batch, z-score lesion rates; aggregate independent chemistries only if preregistered or keep separate axes. The raw codon lesion vector x is then residualized against C plus explicit base-composition, purine/pyrimidine, CpG/UpA, and nearest-neighbor thermodynamic controls; normalize residual to d_resid4.
controls: No tRNA, codon usage, mRNA stability, codon-pair, ribosome, or expression data enter the raw axis.
Identical flanking contexts remove codon-pair and local transcript-context effects at the experimental design stage.
GC, nearest-neighbor chemistry, CpG/UpA, and base-position composition are residualized.
Run DNA-only and RNA-only panels separately; projection must not depend on a single chemistry unless that chemistry was preregistered.
Negative control: replicate the panel with scrambled codon labels before analysis; projection must vanish.
data_sources: bounded 61-sense-codon synthetic DNA oligo panel with identical flanking sequence on both sides of the codon
bounded 61-sense-codon synthetic RNA oligo panel with identical flanking sequence on both sides of the codon
LC-MS, primer-extension, nanopore, or sequencing readouts for UV dimerization, oxidative lesions, hydrolytic deamination, and alkylation under fixed exposure conditions
candidate_axes.failure_mode: Fails if lesion-rate differences are fully explained by GC/base composition or nearest-neighbor chemistry, if replicate variance is too high, if synthesis bias differs by codon, or if no residual projection onto u_SerSplit remains.
candidate_axes.name: matched_trinucleotide_chemical_lesion_residual_axis

tests: TEST_AXIS_ADMISSIBILITY: For each candidate raw vector x, require one finite numeric value for every one of the 61 standard-code sense codons in the locked order. Missing codons, imputed codons not declared before testing, or post-hoc source changes make the candidate inadmissible.

TEST_FORBIDDEN_MATRIX: Build C from intercept, amino-acid one-hot, d_perp_loading, f3_loading, optimal_loading, trna_consensus_loading, trna_supply_tai_centered_loading, GC1, GC2, GC3, total_GC, CpG, UpA, wobble class, codon-family degeneracy, codon-pair incoming/outgoing residuals, mRNA-stability score, ribosome-dwell score, and any candidate-specific nuisance columns. Center and scale non-binary columns; drop linearly dependent columns by QR with locked tolerance 1e-10; set P_C=C(C^T C)^+C^T.

TEST_RESIDUALIZATION: For each x, compute r=(I-P_C)x. Reject if ||r||_2 <= 1e-12 or if any forbidden covariate predicts r in leave-one-source cross-validation with adjusted R2 >= 0.05. Define d_resid4=r/||r||_2 only after this rejection check is passed.

TEST_U_SERSPLIT: Let S4={UCU,UCC,UCA,UCG} and S2={AGU,AGC}. Define u_i=1/sqrt(12) for codons in S4, u_i=-2/sqrt(12) for codons in S2, and u_i=0 otherwise, in the locked 61-codon order. Compute u_r=(I-P_C)u. If ||u_r||_2 <= 1e-12, the SerSplit projection is not testable under the chosen controls. Otherwise define v=u_r/||u_r||_2 and rho=<d_resid4,v>; rho_abs=abs(rho).

TEST_WITHIN_SER_EXACT_NULL: Enumerate all 15 partitions of the six Ser codons into A of size 4 and B of size 2. For each partition define u_A,B with +1/sqrt(12) on A and -2/sqrt(12) on B, residualize by (I-P_C), discard zero residual contrasts, normalize, and compute T_A,B=abs(<d_resid4,v_A,B>). The exact within-Ser p-value is (number of retained partitions with T_A,B >= rho_abs)/(number of retained partitions).

TEST_SIXFOLD_FAMILY_EXACT_NULL: Enumerate every 4-versus-2 partition within each six-codon amino-acid family Ser, Leu, and Arg. Residualize, normalize, and compute absolute projections as above. The exact sixfold-family p-value is the fraction of retained contrasts with projection >= rho_abs. This tests whether the natural Ser split is exceptional relative to same-degeneracy amino-acid families, not whether it is biologically true.

TEST_GLOBAL_MATCHED_SUPPORT_NULL: Enumerate or Monte Carlo preregister all disjoint codon sets A,B with |A|=4 and |B|=2 that match the SerSplit contrast on total GC count and wobble-class counts; form the same zero-sum normalized contrast, residualize against C, normalize, and compare absolute projections to rho_abs. If exact enumeration exceeds the locked compute budget, use a stored seed and at least 1000000 matched draws, reported as an approximation rather than exact.

TEST_MULTIPLE_CANDIDATE_CONTROL: Because candidate_axes are generators, apply Holm correction to projection p-values across all admitted axes and all preregistered subaxes. Passing this test is a flag for further audit, not a scientific verdict.

TEST_NEGATIVE_CONTROLS: For each admitted axis, run the route-specific label, position, source, shifted-frame, or pseudo-codon negative controls. A candidate is rejected if any negative control gives a SerSplit projection with the same sign and at least 80% of rho_abs.

TEST_REPRODUCIBILITY: Split each data source by organism, clade, tissue, assay, platform, or batch as applicable. Reconstruct x, r, d_resid4, and rho in each split. Reject if the material projection is caused by one split or if sign is unstable after the sign convention is locked on the training split.

oracle_json.audit_test: Apply TEST_U_SERSPLIT to the residualized axis. Report rho, abs(rho), within-Ser exact p, sixfold-family exact p, global matched-support p, residual norm, and independence diagnostics. Treat any pass only as a candidate-axis flag, not as a scientific verdict.
oracle_json.construction: Restrict to mature tRNA features outside anticodon bases 34,35,36 and outside any annotation explicitly tied to wobble decoding. Encode positions 32,37,38 and non-anticodon body positions as binary modification presence, chemistry-class burden, enzyme-family burden, and evidence-weighted modification burden. Within each organism, z-score feature columns across tRNA isodecoders. Map each tRNA to directly cognate standard-code codons using the locked codon table. Aggregate multiple isodecoders per codon by median, then aggregate organisms by median or random-effects mean to obtain a finite 61-vector x. Residualize x against the forbidden-control matrix C containing intercept, amino-acid one-hot, tRNA supply/tAI, tRNA consensus loading, f3/ramp, d_perp, optimal loading, GC1, GC2, GC3, total GC, CpG, UpA, wobble class, codon-pair incoming/outgoing scores, mRNA-stability score, and ribosome-dwell score. If r=(I-P_C)x is nonzero, define d_resid4=r/||r||_2.
controls: Exclude anticodon-position and wobble-decoding modification features before construction, not merely after regression.
Use tRNA abundance, tAI, gene copy, and consensus loading only as forbidden controls, never as raw-axis inputs.
Reject if the residual axis is predictable from tRNA supply, f3/ramp, d_perp, GC, wobble, codon-pair effects, mRNA stability, or ribosome dwell with held-out adjusted R2 >= 0.05.
Run leave-one-organism, leave-one-clade, and leave-one-enzyme-family audits.
Negative controls: permute modification positions within tRNA bodies and permute anticodon labels within isotype; both must lose the u_SerSplit projection.
data_sources: MODOMICS tRNA modification records: organism, tRNA isotype, anticodon, mature-position number, modification identity, enzyme, evidence type
GtRNAdb 2.0 or tRNADB-CE tRNA gene/isodecoder records: organism, tRNA ID, isotype, anticodon, predicted mature sequence, decoded codon set
locked standard-code 61-sense-codon table from codon_q6_selection_vectors.v1
oracle_json.failure_mode: Fails if Ser UCN or AGY coverage is sparse, if the residual norm is near zero after forbidden controls, if the projection is driven by anticodon/wobble annotations or tRNA abundance, or if leave-one-source audits make the projection unstable.

oracle_json.audit_test: Apply TEST_U_SERSPLIT to the residual kinetic axis. Also split public-only versus fill-in-only, and lock the sign convention on one split before checking the other.
oracle_json.construction: Use only wild-type, full-length, cognate aminoacylation assays. Exclude anticodon mutants, minihelix-only assays, noncognate mischarging assays, abundance proxies, and assays lacking codon-resolvable tRNA assignment. Convert kcat/Km to log10 units. Within each organism-aaRS-assay-method block, subtract the amino-acid-specific median and divide by MAD. Map each tRNA substrate to directly decoded standard codon(s); if a tRNA decodes multiple synonymous codons, assign only when the decoding set is preregistered and codon-resolvable, otherwise mark missing. Aggregate replicates by inverse-variance weighted mean, isodecoders by median, and organisms by random-effects mean to obtain x over 61 codons. Residualize x against C and set d_resid4=(I-P_C)x/||(I-P_C)x||_2 if admissible.
controls: Amino-acid one-hot columns in C remove amino-acid-level effects, including any Ser-level charging effect.
Anticodon-mutant and wobble-engineering assays are excluded from x.
Assay batch, organism, temperature, pH, and method are normalized before codon aggregation.
tRNA supply/tAI, tRNA consensus, f3/ramp, d_perp, GC, wobble, codon-pair, mRNA-stability, and ribosome-dwell controls are residualized after aggregation.
Coverage gate: every sense codon must have direct or preregistered fill-in kinetic support; post-hoc imputation is not allowed.
data_sources: BRENDA and SABIO-RK aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase kinetic records: enzyme, organism, tRNA substrate, amino acid, kcat, Km, kcat/Km, temperature, pH, buffer, assay method
primary-literature extraction table for wild-type full-length cognate tRNA aminoacylation assays
bounded fill-in kinetic panel if public coverage is incomplete: at least one directly assigned mature cognate tRNA substrate for each of the 61 sense codons
oracle_json.failure_mode: Fails if fewer than 61 codons have direct kinetic support, if Ser codon values are inferred only from anticodon or wobble identity, if organism/method effects dominate, or if amino-acid and tRNA controls remove the residual projection.
oracle_json.name: aaRS_charging_kinetics_residual_axis

oracle_json.audit_test: Apply TEST_U_SERSPLIT to the EF-Tu/EF1A residual axis. Require the same nonzero sign in at least two independent assay sources, or in one public source and the bounded fill-in panel, before flagging the route for further audit.

Candidate-only boundary: I would treat every route below as a generator of an auditable 61-codon vector, not as evidence that the Stop/Ser graph defect is biologically certified. A route only becomes admissible after it produces a finite value for every standard-code sense codon and after the raw vector is residualized against the full forbidden block.
Common admissibility contract
Let the codon order be the locked 61-row sense-only order from codon_q6_selection_vectors.v1. For any proposed raw codon vector  $x\in\mathbb{R}^{61}$ , build a forbidden-control matrix  $C$  with:

$$C=[1,\ \text{amino-acid one-hot},\ d_\perp,\ f3/ramp,\ \text{optimal},\ \text{tRNA consensus},\ \text{tRNA supply/tAI},\ GC_1,GC_2,GC_3,GC_{\rm total},\ CpG,\ UpA,\ \text{wobble class},\ \text{codon-pair in/out},\ \text{mRNA stability},\ \text{ribosome dwell},\ \text{route-specific nuisance columns}]$$

Do not use the local edge-defect decomposition, q6_label, q6_bits, Stop codons, or  $u_{\rm SerSplit}$  to construct  $x$ . They can appear only in post-hoc audit reports or optional robustness controls, not in the raw axis factory.
Drop linearly dependent columns in  $C$  by QR/SVD with a locked tolerance, for example  $10^{-10}$ . Define

$$P_C=C(C^\top C)^+C^\top,\quad r_x=(I-P_C)x.$$

The route fails if  $\|r_x\|_2\le 10^{-12}$ . Otherwise,

$$d_{\rm resid4}=\frac{r_x}{\|r_x\|_2}.$$

A stricter independence gate should also be applied: the residual must not be predictably reconstructible from any forbidden block by leave-one-source, leave-one-clade, or leave-one-assay cross-validation. A practical rejection rule is adjusted  $R^2\ge 0.05$  for any forbidden block or for the joint forbidden block after permutation calibration.
Exact projection test for  $u_{\rm SerSplit}$ 
Define the Ser split contrast on the 61 sense codons:

$$S_4=\{UCU,UCC,UCA,UCG\},\quad S_2=\{AGU,AGC\}.$$


$$u_i=
\begin{cases}
1/\sqrt{12}, & i\in S_4\\
-2/\sqrt{12}, & i\in S_2\\
0, & \text{otherwise.}
\end{cases}$$

Residualize the contrast through the same forbidden matrix:

$$u_r=(I-P_C)u.$$

If  $\|u_r\|_2\le 10^{-12}$ , the SerSplit projection is not testable under that control set. Otherwise define

$$v_{\rm SerSplit}=u_r/\|u_r\|_2,\quad \rho=\langle d_{\rm resid4},v_{\rm SerSplit}\rangle,\quad T_{\rm obs}=|\rho|.$$

Use exact nulls rather than asymptotics:


Within-Ser exact null. Enumerate all  $\binom{6}{4}=15$  partitions of the six Ser codons into a 4-set  $A$  and 2-set  $B$ . For each, construct the same zero-sum contrast, residualize by  $I-P_C$ , normalize if nonzero, and compute  $T_j=|\langle d_{\rm resid4},v_j\rangle|$ . The exact p-value is the retained fraction with  $T_j\ge T_{\rm obs}$ .


Sixfold-family exact null. Repeat the same 4-versus-2 enumeration for Ser, Leu, and Arg, the three six-codon amino-acid families. This tests whether the Ser partition is exceptional relative to same-degeneracy families.


Global matched-support null. Enumerate, or preregister a seeded Monte Carlo draw of at least  $10^6$  contrasts, over disjoint codon sets  $A,B$  with  $|A|=4,|B|=2$ , matched to the Ser contrast on total GC, position-wise GC, wobble-class counts, and degeneracy class where feasible. Residualize and compare absolute projections.


A route “passes” only as a candidate-axis flag: finite axis constructed, forbidden-block residual nonzero, independence audits passed, exact projection detected. It still does not certify the graph-theoretic defect biologically.

Strongest candidate routes
1. Matched-flank chemical lesion residual axis
This is the cleanest non-translation route because the raw signal can be generated without tRNAs, ribosomes, codon usage, transcript abundance, or protein selection.
Finite data source. Synthesize a 61-oligo DNA panel and a 61-oligo RNA panel. Each oligo has identical flanking sequence and differs only in the central sense codon. Run fixed-condition chemical lesion assays: UV dimerization, oxidative damage, alkylation, deamination, and optionally ribose/backbone cleavage for RNA.
Required fields. Codon, full oligo sequence, DNA/RNA flag, chemistry, exposure dose, time, buffer, temperature, molecule count, lesion count, readout method, replicate, batch, synthesis QC, purity, barcode, and blinded codon-label key.
Construction. For each chemistry, estimate a lesion rate or hazard:

$$x_{i,c}=\log\frac{\text{lesion}_{i,c}+1/2}{\text{molecules}_{i,c}+1}.$$

Normalize within chemistry and batch by z-score or batch random effect. Aggregate preregistered chemistries either separately or by inverse-variance mean. Residualize against  $C$  plus nearest-neighbor thermodynamic terms, CpG/UpA, purine/pyrimidine position indicators, and synthesis-QC covariates.
Why it is not explained by forbidden axes. The raw measurement has no tRNA supply, no f3/ramp, no codon-pair context beyond identical flanks, no mRNA stability model, and no ribosome dwell. GC and nearest-neighbor chemistry are explicitly residualized.
Exclusion controls. Reject oligos with failed synthesis QC. Keep codon labels blinded until rates are frozen. Run scrambled-label negative controls. Repeat with at least two flank backgrounds to test whether any projection is flank-specific.
Failure mode. Most of the signal may be base composition or nearest-neighbor chemistry. If residualization removes the vector, the route fails cleanly.
Why this is high value. It gives a codon-level residual axis that is physically real but translation-independent. If it projects onto SerSplit, it is not a tRNA-supply or ribosome-dwell artifact; if it fails, the audit is still decisive.

2. Synonymous DNA damage/repair/mutability residual axis
This route uses natural genetic variation but aims to isolate codon-level mutability rather than selection or translation. gnomAD v4 is large enough to support rare-variant codon opportunity calculations; its v4 release reported 807,162 total individuals, split into exome and genome callsets aligned to GRCh38. GENCODE provides current human/mouse annotation releases and states its goal as identifying and classifying gene features with high accuracy based on biological evidence. gnomAD+1
Finite data sources. gnomAD rare synonymous SNVs, a de novo mutation catalog with callable masks, GENCODE or RefSeq CDS annotations, methylation/CpG tracks, replication timing, trinucleotide mutability model, local callability, and gene constraint annotations.
Required fields. Codon, transcript ID, CDS coordinate, reference codon, alternate codon, synonymous consequence, allele count, allele number, callable opportunity, strand, local trinucleotide, methylation flag, replication timing, expression/callability, gene constraint, splice distance, regulatory-overlap flag.
Construction. Count rare synonymous SNVs by reference codon per callable codon occurrence. Fit an expected neutral mutation model using noncoding or fourfold-degenerate sites:

$$E[\text{SNV}]\sim \text{trinucleotide}+\text{methylation}+\text{strand}+\text{replication timing}+\text{callability}+\text{gene constraint}.$$

For each codon, compute a standardized residual burden:

$$x_i=\frac{O_i-E_i}{\sqrt{E_i+\epsilon}}.$$

Residualize  $x$  against  $C$  plus CpG, UpA, trinucleotide opportunity, and methylation.
Why it is not explained by forbidden axes. The raw mechanism is DNA mutability/repair, not translation efficiency. tRNA supply, f3/ramp,  $d_\perp$ , wobble, codon-pair, mRNA stability, and ribosome dwell enter only as forbidden controls.
Exclusion controls. Exclude splice-proximal, disease-enriched, low-callability, overlapping regulatory, RNA-editing, and repetitive regions. Repeat using de novo-only mutations. Repeat after removing CpG-containing codons.
Failure mode. If GC/trinucleotide/CpG explains everything, the residual vanishes. If de novo-only data do not agree directionally with population rare variants, treat the axis as likely selection- or ascertainment-contaminated.

3. Coding RNA editing and mRNA base-modification residual axis
This is a transcript-chemistry route. It is more biological than the synthetic lesion axis but still not a tRNA-supply, ramp, or dwell axis if handled carefully. RMBase v3.0 describes itself as integrating large epitranscriptome sequencing data and reports 73 RNA modification types across 62 species and 1,074,100 modification sites; RMBase v2 also documents modification-site, motif, RBP, and SNV-related modules. RNA Lab+1
Finite data sources. RMBase v3, m6A-Atlas/DirectRMDB if available, REDIportal/RADAR-style RNA-editing calls, GENCODE CDS annotation, matched RNA-seq coverage, tissue expression, mRNA half-life, local RNA structure, motif scores, RBP-density tracks, known DNA-variant masks.
Required fields. Transcript ID, genome coordinate, CDS coordinate, codon, codon position, modification/editing type, editing or modification level, coverage, confidence, tissue/cell type, platform, expression, local motif, strand, DNA-variant exclusion status, mRNA half-life, predicted local structure.
Construction. Map high-confidence CDS events to codon identity. For each codon, compute an opportunity-normalized event burden:

$$x_i=\operatorname{median}_{tissue,platform}\left[
\log\frac{\text{events}_{i}+1/2}{\text{callable expressed codon opportunities}_{i}+1}
\right].$$

Build separate raw axes for A-to-I editing, C-to-U editing, m6A, m5C, pseudouridine, and a preregistered combined modification burden. Normalize within tissue/platform before codon aggregation. Residualize against  $C$  plus expression, editable-base opportunity, local motif, mRNA half-life, local structure, and RBP density.
Why it is not explained by forbidden axes. It measures editing/modification propensity after controlling expression, motifs, stability, and structure. mRNA stability is a nuisance column, not the axis.
Exclusion controls. Remove known genomic SNPs, low-read-depth calls, mapping-ambiguous sites, repetitive regions, and sites not confidently in CDS. Run +1 and +2 shifted reading-frame pseudo-codon controls. Run tissue leave-one-out and platform leave-one-out audits.
Failure mode. Very likely confounded by base motif and transcript structure. If the SerSplit projection survives only one tissue, one platform, or one modification caller, reject.

4. Genetic-code reassignment/lability residual axis
This route asks whether a standard-code sense codon has independently changed assignment across known or screened genetic codes after removing GC, codon disappearance, tRNA-loss, and wobble mechanisms. NCBI’s genetic-code table lists the standard code and alternative codes, gives a last-update date of September 23, 2024, and explains that its displayed tables use T rather than U for GenBank convention. ncbi.nlm.nih.gov
